title: Top 10 Event Badge Printing Software for B2B Event Teams | Zuddl Blog
summary: Compare 10 event badge printing tools across badge customization, hardware fulfillment, and CRM integration. Covers strengths, gaps, pricing, and fit.
body_markdown:
‍


Your conference starts in 40 minutes. Registration exported the attendee list to a CSV last night, but three VIP speakers corrected their titles this morning. The badge file is stale. Someone is handwriting name corrections on pre-printed badges while 200 attendees watch from the queue.


Badge printing software for B2B events manages more than ink on cardstock. It sits between registration data, onsite hardware logistics, attendee segmentation, CRM workflows, and the first physical impression your brand makes. The platform determines whether VIP badges look distinct from general admission, whether walk-ins get a printed badge or a handwritten label, and whether check-in data reaches your sales team before the closing keynote.


This article evaluates 10 badge printing platforms across badge design customization, onsite hardware fulfillment, and real-time CRM integration after check-in. Each entry covers what the tool does well for B2B event teams, where it falls short, pricing, and the specific team situation it fits.

## The 10 best event badge printing software for B2B Event Teams


### Zuddl


Zuddl is an AI-native unified events platform where badge design, check-in, hardware logistics, and CRM data flow operate from a single system. It fits B2B event teams running conferences and field events across multiple cities who need one provider for the full onsite stack.


**What it does well**


- A[visual badge editor](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/onsite-events/event-check-in-and-badge-printing) lets teams apply custom fonts per field, use merge tags to auto-populate attendee data (name, title, company), choose between paper or plastic badge materials, and select vertical or horizontal orientation. Badge settings are tied to audience groups assigned at registration, so VIP badges differ from general admission by configuration rather than manual workaround.
- Zuddl acts as single point of contact for arranging all[onsite equipment: badge stock, lanyards, printers, iPads, kiosk stands, and routers](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/onsite-events) . For teams running 40 or more field events across multiple cities, this eliminates per-event equipment procurement. Backup printers are included in every hardware fulfillment package.
- Check-in supports self-serve kiosks, staff-operated assisted check-in, and QR code scanning within the same event. General attendees use kiosks while VIP attendees receive staff-assisted check-in. The system handles 500 or more check-ins during a morning rush without requiring 10 staffed registration desks.
- The onsite app caches the full attendee list locally before the event. Check-in and badge printing continue operating without an internet connection. A dedicated onsite support team assists with setup, testing, and live issue resolution on event day.
- When an attendee checks in, real-time Slack alerts notify account executives that a target account has arrived.[Bi-directional Salesforce sync](https://www.zuddl.com/event-integrations) updates CRM records with check-in status, and Zuddl surfaces which attendees are high-priority opportunities.[Session-level attendance data feeds lead scoring](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/onsite-events/session-management) across Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, and Eloqua.


**Where it has gaps**


- Buyers anchored to lower-cost point solutions or free incumbents may view Zuddl’s pricing as a net-new cost rather than a replacement. The platform is positioned for teams that value brand control and unified data, not for budget-first buyers.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.[Request a demo](https://www.zuddl.com/pricing)


**Ratings:** 4.8/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B event teams running conferences and field events across multiple cities who want a single vendor for badge design, hardware fulfillment, offline-capable check-in, and real-time CRM intelligence, replacing a stack of disconnected point solutions.


### vFairs


vFairs provides on-demand badge printing with a drag-and-drop editor, bundled hardware rental, and onsite technician support. It serves teams running large conferences and trade shows that need vendor-managed equipment alongside broad printer compatibility.


**What it does well**


- The badge editor supports single and double-sided badges with custom fonts, sizes, colors, positioning, logos, QR codes, and custom fields. Badge designs can be segmented by user type, including staff, exhibitors, and speakers.
- Hardware rentals are bundled with the event management software. Certified vFairs technicians provide onsite support for real-time assistance with setup, connectivity, and equipment issues during the event.
- The platform supports Zebra, Epson, HP, and Brother printers, giving organizations with existing hardware inventory a path to use what they already own rather than renting new equipment.
- Check-in includes QR code scanning and facial recognition. Facial recognition reduces queue times at high-volume entry points when advance configuration is completed.


**Where it has gaps**


- Advanced badge design changes sometimes require contacting the vFairs support team rather than being fully self-serve in the platform.
- Real-time CRM sync (as opposed to post-event batch export) requires additional configuration and is not available out of the box for all plans. Native Slack notifications for sales reps on check-in are not a highlighted feature and require custom integration work.
- Facial recognition setup requires advance configuration and can slow check-in if not properly tested before event day.
- Hardware rental costs add meaningfully to the total event budget and are not always transparent upfront during the sales process.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.7/5 on G2 · 4.8/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B conference teams running large-format events (trade shows, multi-track conferences) who want bundled hardware rental with onsite technician backup and broad printer brand compatibility, and who can accept that advanced badge design and CRM integration may require vendor support involvement.


### Cvent


Cvent’s OnArrival check-in and badge printing module generates badges dynamically from registration data with walk-in support and last-minute update handling. It fits enterprise conference teams already operating within the Cvent ecosystem for registration and event management.


**What it does well**


- OnArrival prints badges on-demand from live registration data. Walk-in registrations and real-time attendee detail modifications are handled at the door without pre-printed badge tables.
- The OnArrival 360 full-service model includes hardware, kiosks, printers, and onsite Cvent technicians. Enterprise conference teams running events with 1,000 or more attendees cite this managed service as a key reason for choosing Cvent.
- Self-serve kiosks and staffed check-in stations run in parallel at large events. QR code scanning is supported at entry points for high-volume morning rushes.
- Session check-in with badge scanning supports capacity control and continuing education credit tracking. Session attendance data feeds post-event reporting for content team planning.


**Where it has gaps**


- The self-service Event-in-a-Box tier requires buyers to source and manage compatible hardware independently. Onsite technician support, backup printers, and managed hardware are only available through the OnArrival 360 managed service at higher cost.
- The badge design interface is described by reviewers as clunky and requiring significant setup time. Advanced customization (custom fonts, precise layout control) may require Cvent’s professional services team rather than self-serve configuration.
- Salesforce integration exists, but reviewers report that data sync is not truly real-time. Check-in data arrives in CRM with a lag that limits same-day follow-up during the event. Native Slack notifications for sales reps on check-in are not a documented feature.
- Teams running frequent field events across multiple cities note that Cvent’s hardware model is designed for single large conferences, not distributed event programs.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.3/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Enterprise conference teams already running registration through Cvent who need managed onsite badge printing and check-in at scale, and who have the budget for the OnArrival 360 full-service tier rather than the self-service kit.


### Expo Pass


Expo Pass positions itself as an onsite badge printing provider that owns the full badge experience, from its own print shop to the software and hardware. It serves teams that want a complete shipped kit without sourcing equipment independently.


**What it does well**


- Badge printing kits come with everything needed for onsite check-in: iPad kiosks, Zebra thermal printers, and network-redundant routers. Setup is plug-and-play, reducing configuration time compared to assembling components from multiple vendors.
- On-demand badge printing produces full-color output with support for 4x3 and 4x6 badge sizes, custom branding, and professional conference lanyards. Thermal printing eliminates ink-related failures on event day.
- Registration data syncs to badge printing with walk-in handling and on-site info changes processed at the check-in kiosk. Reviewers cite the ability to make name corrections at the door without reprinting from a stale list.


**Where it has gaps**


- The platform is effectively locked to the Expo Pass hardware kit. Organizations with existing Zebra or Brother printer inventory cannot easily substitute their own equipment, which creates cost friction for teams that already own printers.
- Advanced badge design customization for audience-segment-specific tiers (VIP vs. general) requires working with the Expo Pass team rather than self-serve configuration in the platform.
- Native CRM integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot) are limited or require third-party connectors. Post-event data export is primarily CSV-based, with no real-time sales alerts or Slack notifications. Check-in data reaching CRM requires manual export and import steps.
- True offline-cache functionality (operating without any internet) is not explicitly documented. The network-redundant router is the primary resilience mechanism rather than a locally cached attendee list.


**Pricing:** Packages start at $2,495.


**Ratings:** 4.7/5 on G2 · 4.8/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B event teams that do not own badge printing hardware and want a fully shipped kit with thermal printers, branded lanyards, and kiosks included, accepting that equipment substitution and CRM integration depth are limited.


### Accelevents


Accelevents offers a no-code badge designer with per-registration-type badge assignment and multi-kiosk self-serve check-in. It fits mid-market teams that can source or rent their own printer hardware and want a self-serve badge design workflow.


**What it does well**


- The badge designer supports starting from a template or a blank canvas. Unique badge layouts can be assigned per ticket or registration category (attendees, VIPs, speakers, staff, exhibitors). Merge tags auto-populate attendee data, and QR codes are added via drag-and-drop.
- Multiple kiosks can connect to the badge printer setup simultaneously, keeping lines moving during peak arrivals. Attendees scan, confirm, and print their badge in seconds at a self-serve kiosk.
- Printers can be ordered or rented through Accelevents or trusted partners, or teams can bring their own printers. Zebra thermal printers are cited as the most compatible option. Color printing through PrintNode is available with compatible inkjet or PVC printers.


**Where it has gaps**


- No vendor-supplied full hardware stack (iPads, routers, lanyards, stands, badge stock) or onsite technician dispatch is documented. Buyers coordinate hardware sourcing independently or through Accelevents partners.
- Offline check-in and badge printing capability is not documented on vendor product pages. Reviewers note concerns about reliability when venue WiFi is unstable.
- Session-level check-in, access control, and real-time CRM integration (Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack alerts) are not documented on the badge printing or pricing pages reviewed.


**Pricing:** Starting from $7,500/event (Professional plan).


**Ratings:** 4.7/5 on G2 · 4.7/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Mid-market B2B event teams that own or can rent Zebra printers and want a self-serve badge designer with per-attendee-type layouts, accepting that hardware fulfillment, offline mode, and CRM integration require separate solutions.


### Whova


Whova provides a drag-and-drop badge editor with 17 ready-to-use templates and on-demand printing triggered by check-in. It fits conference organizers who already own Zebra or Brother printers and want badge printing as part of a broader event app platform.


**What it does well**


- The drag-and-drop badge editor supports logos, images, custom fields, and QR codes for lead retrieval and contact exchange. Badge customization by attendee category is available onsite.
- On-demand badge printing triggers automatically when an attendee checks in. Walk-ins receive a printed badge through real-time badge generation. A central badge printing queue supports multi-device check-in across several iPads.
- The platform works with Zebra and Brother printers, covering most organizations’ existing hardware investments without requiring new equipment purchases.


**Where it has gaps**


- No hardware fulfillment service is available. Buyers source, ship, and set up their own printers, iPads, and networking equipment. Reviewers who expected turnkey onsite equipment were disappointed.
- No distinct VIP or tiered check-in mode is documented. All attendee types go through the same self-serve kiosk check-in flow without a separate staff-assisted lane for executive attendees.
- Offline check-in capability is not explicitly claimed on vendor product pages. Reviewers running events in venues with poor connectivity describe uncertainty around system reliability.
- Real-time CRM sync (Salesforce, HubSpot) is not cited as a native capability. Attendance data flows via post-event CSV export, and no Slack or sales alert integration for check-in events is documented.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.8/5 on G2 · 4.8/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Conference organizers who already own Zebra or Brother printers and want badge printing bundled into an event app with networking and attendee engagement features, accepting that hardware logistics, VIP check-in differentiation, and CRM data flow are handled outside the platform.


### Nunify


Nunify offers a visual badge designer with Zebra and Apple AirPrint support, and explicitly claims fully offline badge printing with no WiFi required. It fits teams running events at venues where internet connectivity is unreliable or absent.


**What it does well**


- Badge printing works fully offline with no WiFi needed. This is an explicit vendor claim, not a fallback mode, making it distinct from platforms that rely on network-redundant routers or cached attendee lists as secondary mechanisms.
- QR code scanning and attendee verification print a badge in 3 seconds. An iPad or kiosk mode supports check-in across multiple locations with a real-time dashboard.
- The platform holds SOC-2, ISO 27001, GDPR, CCPA, and PCI compliance certifications, addressing data governance requirements for regulated industries.


**Where it has gaps**


- No onsite hardware fulfillment, equipment shipping, or vendor-supplied technician support is documented. Buyers source their own printers and devices.
- Reviewers report wanting more control over badge layout and branding elements. Audience-segment-specific badge logic (VIP vs. general) and template inheritance across events are not documented.
- Real-time CRM integration (Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack alerts) and session-level check-in or access control are not documented on vendor pages.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** Not available on G2 · 4.8/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B event teams running events at venues with known WiFi limitations (hotels, restaurants, off-site field locations) who prioritize confirmed offline badge printing over hardware fulfillment or CRM integration depth.


### EventPack


EventPack provides a badge designer with variable data support, offline check-in capability, and a credits-based pricing model. It fits teams managing recurring events who want to avoid per-event pricing.


**What it does well**


- The system works offline, and data syncs automatically once connectivity is restored. This removes venue WiFi dependency for check-in and badge printing operations.
- Multiple check-in options (QR code, name search, manual entry) and a customizable kiosk mode allow attendees to self-check-in. Real-time tracking lets teams monitor check-ins from a command center.
- Session scanning tracks who attends each session and monitors session capacity, providing breakout-level attendance data beyond event-entry check-in.


**Where it has gaps**


- No vendor-managed hardware fulfillment, equipment shipping, or onsite technician support is documented. Buyers source all printers and devices independently.
- No specific printer brands or models (Zebra, Brother) are named. The vendor claims compatibility with a “wide range” of printers without confirming which brands are supported.
- CRM integration is limited to HubSpot sync and Zapier connections (3,000+ apps). No Salesforce native integration, real-time sales alerts, or session-level CRM enrichment is documented.
- Audience-segment-specific badge logic (VIP vs. general vs. speaker) and template inheritance across events are not documented on vendor pages.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** Not available on G2 · Not available on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B event teams managing a recurring calendar of events who want credits-based check-in pricing and offline reliability, and who can tolerate sourcing their own hardware and managing CRM data flow through Zapier or HubSpot connectors.


### idloom


idloom is a European event management platform with a badge module that supports unlimited badge dimensions and per-guest-type badge configuration. It fits teams running registration-heavy events who want badge design tied to guest categories at a predictable monthly cost.


**What it does well**


- Badge layouts are customizable with unlimited dimensions and designs. Multiple badge types can be configured per registration type or guest category (e.g., different badges for regular guests, speakers, and press).
- QR codes and barcodes are supported on badges for entry scans. Badge printing and access control connect in one workflow. PDF badges can be sent automatically in confirmation emails for attendee self-printing.
- Published pricing starts at €150/month with no per-ticket, per-attendee, or per-registrant fees. A free tier and 15-day trial are available.


**Where it has gaps**


- No onsite hardware fulfillment, equipment shipping, or named printer brand compatibility is documented. Buyers source their own printers and devices.
- No offline check-in or badge printing mode is documented. No onsite technician support or backup equipment programs are mentioned.
- CRM and marketing automation integration is not documented on product or pricing pages. Reviewers note that integration options with external tools could be improved.
- Reviewers describe badge and event page customization as constrained for advanced branding needs, requiring workarounds for complex design requirements.


**Pricing:** Starting from €150/month (Light plan). Premium from €550/month. Corporate at €1,150/month. All billed annually.


**Ratings:** 4.6/5 on G2 · 4.8/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** European B2B event teams running frequent registration-heavy events who want per-guest-type badge configuration at a fixed monthly cost, and who handle their own onsite hardware and do not require CRM integration or offline capability from their badge software.


### Eventbrite


Eventbrite is a ticketing and event discovery platform with a mobile check-in app for QR code scanning. It does not offer native badge printing, badge design, or onsite hardware support. Teams needing printed badges must layer a third-party tool on top.


**What it does well**


- The mobile organizer app supports QR code scanning for staff-assisted check-in at the door. Walk-in attendees can be added via the app during the event.
- Free to publish unlimited events. Per-ticket fees (3.7% + $1.79 per paid ticket) replace upfront platform costs for teams with limited budgets.


**Where it has gaps**


- Badge design and badge printing are not native features. There is no badge designer, no template system, no QR-code-on-badge generation, and no audience-segment badge differentiation.
- No onsite hardware (printers, iPads, routers, badge stock) is supplied, shipped, or managed by Eventbrite.
- No self-serve kiosk mode is offered. Check-in is limited to staff-operated mobile scanning with no parallel lanes or VIP differentiation.
- No offline check-in mode, onsite technician support, or session-level check-in is available.
- CRM connectivity (Salesforce, HubSpot) relies on Zapier or basic integrations. No real-time sales alerts or session-level data flow is documented.


**Pricing:** Free base plan. Per-ticket fees of 3.7% + $1.79 per paid ticket, plus 2.9% payment processing per order.


**Ratings:** 4.4/5 on G2 · 4.6/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Teams using Eventbrite for ticket sales and event discovery who accept that badge printing, onsite hardware, offline check-in, and CRM intelligence all require separate tools layered on top of the platform.


## What to look for in event badge printing software for B2B Event Teams


**Badge design customization.** Evaluate whether the platform supports per-audience-segment badge logic (VIP, speaker, sponsor, general), custom fonts, QR codes, and template reuse across events. Without this, every event starts from scratch, and attendee tiers are visually indistinguishable at the door.


**Registration-to-badge data connection.** Confirm that badge printing pulls from live registration data without CSV exports. Test walk-in handling and last-minute name corrections. A stale export means every badge printed after a correction is wrong.


**Onsite hardware and equipment fulfillment.** Determine whether the vendor supplies, ships, and retrieves printers, iPads, routers, badge stock, and lanyards, or whether your team sources everything independently. For distributed event programs across multiple cities, per-event procurement consumes disproportionate operational capacity.


**Check-in throughput and mode flexibility.** Verify that the platform supports parallel self-serve kiosks and staff-assisted check-in within the same event. A single check-in mode forces VIP executives into the same queue as general attendees.


**Printer hardware compatibility and flexibility.** Check which printer brands (Zebra, Brother, Epson) are natively supported. A platform locked to one brand forces teams to replace existing hardware or rent at elevated per-event cost.


**Offline reliability and event-day resilience.** Confirm whether check-in and badge printing continue without internet connectivity. Venue WiFi failures are common. A platform with no offline mode reverts your team to paper lists and handwritten badges.


**Session check-in and access control.** Evaluate whether badge-based check-in extends to individual sessions with capacity enforcement and ticket-tier access gating. Without this, premium sessions cannot be restricted, and session attendance data is unavailable for content planning.


**Post-check-in CRM integration and real-time attendee intelligence.** Verify whether[check-in data flows to your CRM in real time, triggering sales alerts when target accounts arrive](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-analytics) . Batch export the day after the event is too late for same-day follow-up when engagement is highest.


## Questions people ask about event badge printing software


**What should event badge printing software integrate with?**


At minimum, it should connect to your registration system (to pull attendee data live), your CRM (Salesforce or HubSpot), and your marketing automation platform. Strong setups also[push check-in events to Slack so sales reps receive real-time alerts](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/universal-lead-capture) when target accounts arrive. Without CRM integration, attendance data stays siloed and follow-up happens too late.


**What is the difference between onsite badge printing and pre-printed badges?**


Pre-printed badges are produced before the event from a static attendee list. Any name correction, ticket transfer, or walk-in after the print run creates a mismatch. Onsite badge printing generates each badge at the moment of check-in from live registration data, so the printed output always reflects the current attendee record. For B2B events with late registrations and VIP changes, onsite printing eliminates the stale-data problem.


**How do you choose the best event badge printing software for your event size?**


For single large conferences (500+ attendees), prioritize high-throughput check-in with parallel kiosk and staff lanes, onsite technician support, and session-level access control. For distributed field event programs across multiple cities, prioritize single-vendor hardware fulfillment and offline reliability. Zuddl covers both scenarios. Cvent’s OnArrival 360 is strong for single enterprise conferences. Expo Pass works for teams that want a shipped hardware kit.


**Can event badge printing software handle last-minute registrations and walk-ins?**


Most platforms in this list support on-the-spot registration and on-demand badge printing at the check-in desk. The key differentiator is whether walk-in data syncs back to the registration system and CRM automatically, or whether it requires a manual export step after the event. Platforms with live registration-to-badge connections process walk-ins without disrupting the check-in queue. Platforms that rely on pre-exported attendee lists cannot print accurate badges for late registrants.
